definition: The amount of solute, in moles, in each cubic decimetre of solution (not of solvent), measured in $\pu{mol dm-3}$ and written in square brackets, as in $[\ce{NaCl}]$.
A solution whose concentration is known accurately, usually made by dissolving a weighed mass of solute and making it up to the mark in a volumetric flask.
Adding more solvent to a solution, which lowers its concentration while the amount of solute in moles stays the same, so $C_1V_1 = C_2V_2$.
The rule that gases at the same temperature and pressure have the same number of molecules in equal volumes, so the volume of a gas is proportional to its amount in moles.
